project_overview: This project appears to be a single-page application (SPA) likely built with Vue.js, focused on user dashboards and data management. The core structure consists of several Vue components responsible for different sections of the user interface, including user profiles, product displays, and admin settings. The dependency graph suggests a relatively simple component-based architecture, with components primarily relying on 'Router push' navigation. However, the lack of explicit dependencies between many components raises concerns about maintainability and potential fragility.

layers.description: Vue components responsible for rendering the user interface.
Handles navigation and routing within the application.

macro_trends.title: Potential State Management Fragility
macro_trends.description: The lack of defined dependencies between components suggests potential state management challenges. Without clear state ownership and management strategies, components may inadvertently modify state in other parts of the application, leading to unpredictable behavior and difficult debugging.

macro_trends.title: Router Dependency Over-Reliance
macro_trends.description: The primary navigation method appears to be 'Router push', which concentrates navigation logic within the Router. This may create a point of failure if the Router encounters issues and can introduce coupling between components and the routing mechanism.

key_workflows.name: User Authentication Flow
key_workflows.description: This workflow likely involves the user authenticating via the LoginForm, triggering a state update, and then being navigated to the UserDashboard or UserProfile component based on their roles and permissions.
